reuse.qualification: Only Mayu Maman material UV assignment changed; four other models and every other runtime byte plus their regenerated isolated fixtures match. Reuse excludes Mayu Maman; actions and all presentation runs use the final package.

iterations: Initial contact witnesses on Nowet clothing rims failed independent serialized/posed tests; actual interior overlap witnesses corrected them.

Native views exposed inherited pointed ears, overly long beards, sparse shoulder hair and incomplete front cloth. Rounded ears, short beards, flowing front locks, fuller calves and distinct overlapping panels address those findings.
The added drape/crossing contact witnesses were moved from cap edges to actual shared interior volume. All source iterations and failed diagnostics remain archived.

Native review exposed edge-on cloth panels caused by automatically transported tube axes. Fixed depth/width loft sections preserve intended frontal coverage; native01 is retained as a superseded iteration.
The local exporter retains only the shared pipeline and face material-cell clamp; unused closed-skirt deformation was removed before repeated final exports.

Mayu Maman torso and sash material assignments were adjusted after native02 so the ivory bodice reads as continuous clothing. Her full native03 suite was repeated; reuse01 bounds continuity reuse for the four byte-identical models/fixtures. Actions and every presentation pair use final land04.
reviewed: Native front/profile/rear, face/hair/cloth, extreme strides, attack, pain, intermediate death and lying poses; both presentation scenes per species.
qualifications: Stylized closed component anatomy, painted faces, opaque hair and rigid fall/rest remain candidates. Fixed garments and ornaments do not create modular equipment.

Open-front garments intentionally expose a leg; no closed-skirt containment claim. Provisional collision/statistics/combat/loot/identity/save fields remain authoritative, with no reference metric scale, powers or campaign placement adoption.

One sequential700-tic sprite/model pair per species measures queue presentation intervals and simulation spacing, not GPU/display latency, repeatability, an optimization or campaign/crowd performance.

Coverage reaches48/56 provisional classes;8 remain. Regional displays, other characters/modular fitting, campaign authoring and siege rendering keep the batch unfinished. No author acceptance or final terminal is claimed.

Nowet's first model run had a 296.5928 ms queue-presentation tail and a 221.4049 ms simulation interval. One bounded sequential sprite/model repeat, with no native or validation job in parallel, records a model maximum of 1.5232 ms and simulation maximum of 29.2955 ms. Both runs are retained. The repeat does not identify the cause or establish repeatability or a performance improvement.
